data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company, is currently valued at $1.6B post-money following $1.37B in cumulative fundraising. The valuation assessment draws from a peer set of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector at similar or adjacent stages. Key private peers include Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B, Series B), and Agile Robots ($1.0B, Series C).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $1.6B post-money valuation and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical for Series C to next-stage advancement, implies $2.7B. Peer-median analysis across the six most directly comparable companies yields $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer cohort reflects material stage heterogeneity, with some peers at Series B and others at Series D, introducing moderate dispersion in the comparable set.

Triangulation of these two methods produces a valuation range of $1.4B to $3.1B, with a median of $2.2B. This range positions Hadrian's current $1.6B valuation near the lower end of the triangulated band. Key uncertainties center on the appropriate stage-progression multiple given market conditions and the precise relevance of peers spanning Series B through Series D, which limits confidence in any point estimate.
